title: "Model building"
format: html
---

## Background

Aim: assess predictive accuracy between categories of model structures, accounting for confounding among high-dimensional forecasts

- Outcome: Weighted interval score (WIS; log-transformed accuracy score)
- Exposure of interest: Model method (mechanistic, statistical, etc.)
- Additional exposures:
  - CountryTargets: model predicts for single- vs multi-country
  - Trend: epidemic trend (stable, increasing, decreasing)
  - Incidence: log of current incidence level (smooth)
  - Location: location (random effect)
  - VariantPhase: dominant variant phase (random effect)
  - Horizon: forecast horizon (smooth, by model)
  - Model: individual model (random effect)

## Quick start

Source `analysis-model.R` to load the data, model formulas, and fitting functions.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(here)
source(here("R", "analysis-model.R"))
```

`model_wis()` runs all of the model build in one call: data preparation, univariate and joint fits, effect extraction, and saving outputs.

```{r}
#| label: pipeline
#| eval: false

model_wis(scoring_scale = "log", output_dir = "output/log")
model_wis(scoring_scale = "natural", output_dir = "output/natural")
```

## Full build

This document demonstrates the process of building the GAMM reported in the main analysis.
All functions shown here are defined in `R/analysis-model.R`.
Chunks that fit models are shown but not evaluated.

### Data preparation

`prepare_model_data()` takes the scored forecasts from `process_data()` and prepares them for modelling.
It removes the Hub ensemble and baseline models, drops forecasts without a score, and (when scoring on the log scale) log-transforms incidence to match the scale of the outcome.

```{r}
#| label: data-prep
#| message: false

data <- prepare_model_data(process_data(scoring_scale = "log"),
                           scoring_scale = "log")
count(data, Method)
```

### Outcome distribution and family

We scored forecasts against observations on a log scale.
`wis_family()` matches the model family to the scoring scale, using a Gaussian with log link for log-scale WIS.
Alternatively, we use a Gamma for natural-scale WIS.

```{r}
#| label: family

wis_family(scoring_scale = "log")
```

The choice of log link is examined in a sensitivity analysis (`R/sensitivity/check-link-robustness.R`).

### Unadjusted models

We first fit each covariate on its own to get unadjusted estimates.
Comparing these against the adjusted estimates shows how much each association is explained by the other covariates.
The univariate formulas are held in `m.formulas_uni`, one term each, and fitted with `fit_univariate()`.

```{r}
#| label: uni-formulas

m.formulas_uni
```

```{r}
#| label: fit-uni
#| eval: false

fits_uni <- fit_univariate(data, wis_family("log"))
```

### Joint model

The joint model includes all covariates together, with the formula held in `m.formula_joint`.

```{r}
#| label: joint-formula

m.formula_joint
```

Epidemiological target (cases vs deaths) enters as a fixed parametric term.
Method, CountryTargets, Trend, Location, VariantPhase, and Model are random effects (`bs = "re"`).
Incidence enters as a smooth.
Horizon as a per-model smooth with sum-to-zero constraint (`bs = "sz"`).
`fit_wis()` fits with `mgcv::bam()` using fast REML and discretised covariates for speed.

```{r}
#| label: fit-joint
#| eval: false

fit_joint <- fit_wis(m.formula_joint, data, wis_family("log"))
```

### Extracting effects and diagnostics

`extract_all_effects()` combines the unadjusted (univariate) and adjusted (joint) estimates into one table, including both random and fixed effects.

```{r}
#| label: extract
#| eval: false

effects <- extract_all_effects(fits_uni, fit_joint)
```

`save_model_outputs()` writes the effects and basis-dimension checks (`results.rds`), observed-vs-fitted values (`fit_obs.rds`), and `gratia::appraise()` diagnostic plots to the output directory.

```{r}
#| label: save
#| eval: false

save_model_outputs(fit_joint, data, effects, output_dir = "output/log")
```

And check the results visually.

```{r}
#| label: check-joint

knitr::include_graphics(here("output", "log", "plots", "check_joint.png"))
```

## Results

```{r}
source(here("R", "plot-model-results.R"))
```

Plot absolute WIS.

```{r}
#| label: fig-error-vs-obs
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   Forecast error scales with the magnitude of the observed outcome.
#|   Weighted interval score (WIS) is plotted against observed incidence for COVID-19 cases and deaths across 32 European countries.
#|   Faint points show individual forecasts; lines show a generalised additive model smooth fit per model-structure group, with shaded 95% confidence intervals.
#|   Both axes are shown on the log scale; lower WIS indicates better performance.
#|   Colour: model structure.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 8

# natural-scale scores for descriptive error-vs-observation figure
scores_natural <- process_data(scoring_scale = "log") |>
  filter(!grepl("EuroCOVIDhub-", Model))
plot_error_vs_obs(scores_natural)
```

And show main results.

```{r}
#| label: results-scores-results
#| 
results <- readRDS(here("output", "log", "results.rds"))
print_table2(results$effects)
```

```{r}
plot_effects(results$effects, variables = c("Method"))
```
